question_text: Find the real and imaginary parts of the complex number (a + ib)/(a − ib).

mark_split.label: Multiply above and below by a + ib
Expand and read off the real and imaginary parts

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the real and imaginary parts of this quotient — what you multiply by and what you read off.
insider_note: The multiplier a + ib is the numerator itself, so the top is one known expansion (a + ib)² and the bottom is a² + b², never a² − b². Report the imaginary part as the real number 2ab/(a² + b²), with no i attached.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply by the conjugate
steps.margin_note: First mark. The conjugate of the denominator a − ib is a + ib, the same as the numerator, so the top becomes (a + ib)² and the bottom a² + b².

recall.must_convey: That numerator and denominator are multiplied by a + ib, the conjugate of the denominator, giving (a + ib)² over a² + b².
accept: multiply top and bottom by a plus i b so the denominator is a squared plus b squared and the numerator is a plus i b squared

the bottom becomes a squared plus b squared and the top becomes a plus i b whole square
conjugate a plus i b tho multiply cheste denominator a square plus b square
multiply by the conjugate to make the denominator real

steps.why: (a − ib)(a + ib) = a² + b² is real. Once the denominator is real, the real and imaginary parts of the whole quotient are just the real and imaginary parts of the numerator, each divided by a² + b².
common_mistakes: Multiplying by a − ib, which leaves an i in the denominator.
Writing the denominator as a² − b².

steps.label: Read off the parts
steps.margin_note: Second mark. (a + ib)² = a² + 2abi + i²b² = (a² − b²) + 2abi. Divide each part by a² + b².

recall.must_convey: That expanding gives real part (a² − b²)/(a² + b²) and imaginary part 2ab/(a² + b²).
accept: expand the square, real part is a squared minus b squared over a squared plus b squared and imaginary part is two a b over a squared plus b squared

steps.why: The imaginary part is the real coefficient of i — it is 2ab/(a² + b²), not i·2ab/(a² + b²). Writing the two parts as separate real fractions is the answer the question asks for.
common_mistakes: Writing i²b² as +b² and getting real part 1.
Reporting the imaginary part with the i still attached.
